sonnet.problem: This card tells God's warning that Abimelech is 'as good as dead,' which is a death moment. It still carries a drawer joke ('I'd STILL take that over this'), which puts a joke on a death warning.
sonnet.rule: **Heavy moments.** A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: The card asks about verse 17 (the healing so they can bear children again) right after card 17 asked about verse 18 (the LORD closed all the wombs). The answer to card 18 is already implied by card 17's right answer, since the closed wombs are why they needed healing. It is also a True statement that just repeats a point card 17 made. The cards also run out of passage order: verse 18 is asked before verse 17.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.
